label: EU7-F65
statement: Sertindole | In lists: 3 (A); 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Risk of hypotension, falls, QTc-prolongation | Dose adjustment/special considerations: 10 mg/d. E | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment; risperidone (<6 weeks), olanzapine (<10 mg/d), haloperidol (<2 mg single dose; <5mg/d); quetiapine[d]. E || Ziprasidone | In lists: 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Risk of QTc-prolongation, torsades de pointes, sedation, insomnia and orthostatic hypotension. Not approved for the treatment of dementia-related psychosis. Risk of increased mortality, increased with higher doses, when used for behavioural problems in dementia may be similar to the risk for risperidone | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Starting dose 20 mg/d. E | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment; risperidone (<6 weeks), olanzapine (<10 mg/d), haloperidol (<2 mg single dose; <5mg/d); quetiapine[d]. E || Clozapine | In lists: 3, 4, 5 (A); 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Anticholinergic and extrapyramidal side effects (tardive dyskinesia); parkinsonism; hypotonia; sedation; risk of falling; increased mortality in persons with dementia; increased risk of agranulocytosis and myocarditis | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Start with 12.5 mg/d. E Start low–go slow; reduce dose in cases of significant renal failure. M | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment; risperidone (<6 weeks), olanzapine (<10 mg/d), haloperidol (<2 mg single dose; <5mg/d); quetiapine[d]. E || Olanzapine (>10 mg/d) | In lists: 4, 5 (A); 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Anticholinergic and extrapyramidal side effects (tardive dyskinesia); parkinsonism; hypotonia; sedation; risk of falling; increased mortality in persons with dementia | Dose adjustment/special considerations: (blank: per ESM note, no suggestion by experts or in Micromedex) | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment; risperidone (<6 weeks), olanzapine (<10 mg/d), haloperidol (<2 mg single dose; <5mg/d); quetiapine[d]. E || Risperidone (>6 weeks) | In lists: 5 (A); 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Problematic risk-benefit profile for the treatment of behavioural symptoms of dementia; increased mortality, with higher dose, in patients with dementia | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Use the lowest dose required (0.5-1.5 mg/d) for the shortest time period necessary. E For geriatric patients or in cases of severe renal failure (CrCl <30 mL/min), start with 0.5 mg twice daily; increase doses by 0.5 mg twice daily; increases above 1.5 mg twice daily should be done at intervals of at least 1 week; slower titration may be necessary. For geriatric patients, if once-daily dosing desired, initiate and titrate on a twice-daily regimen for 2 to 3 days to achieve target dose and switch to once-daily dosing thereafter. M | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment; risperidone (<6 weeks), olanzapine (<10 mg/d), haloperidol (<2 mg single dose; <5mg/d); quetiapine[d]. E || Aripiprazole | In lists: 5 (A); 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Risk of increased mortality when used for behavioural problems in dementia | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Use the lowest dose required (7-12mg/d) for the shortest time period necessary. E | Alternatives: Non-pharmacological treatment; risperidone (<6 weeks), olanzapine (<10 mg/d), haloperidol (<2 mg single dose; <5mg/d); quetiapine[d]. E

preambles.text: The aim of the study was to develop a European list of potentially inappropriate medications (PIM) for older people, which can be used for the analysis and comparison of prescribing patterns across European countries and for clinical practice.

preambles.scope: EU(7)-PIM article: dose and alternative suggestions
preambles.text: The PIM list contains suggestions for dose adjustments and therapeutic alternatives. Dose adjustments and drug alternatives suggested by the experts during the Delphi survey were compiled and included in the EU(7)-PIM list, prioritising in each case those made by the higher number of experts. Suggestions were complemented, if necessary, with information available from the other PIM lists and from Micromedex® [[32](http://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4464049/#CR32)], a commercially available database which contains comprehensive information on drug use.

footnotes_and_definitions.text: Caution, this drug was judged to be questionable PIM.
E: Experts; M: Micromedex ® [32]; P: PRISCUS list [22]; L: Laroche et al (2007) [3]; McL: McLeod et al (1997) [26]; B: Beers list (2012) [18].
Note: if nothing is stated under “Dose adjustment / special considerations of use”, this means that no suggestion was made either by the experts or in Micromedex® .

'In lists' gives the numbered prior PIM lists in which the substance appears, with Category A (precisely this active substance is named as a PIM) or Category B (a PIM only in certain clinical conditions or comorbidities, or not named but covered as a PIM drug class). 'Does not appear as PIM' means the substance was not a PIM in those prior lists; it is still an entry of the EU(7)-PIM list and is not an exclusion. Entries the panel judged questionable carry footnote d.
footnotes_and_definitions.source: EU(7)-PIM ESM1 legend (footnotes a and d)
